claim: R5-08 (a) gave every crisis line form a key, and V09 §4.21.12 (4) words a look on the why card of a building it stands over by `info.crisis.ruinedFor` 'in the form the line takes: `ruinedForOpen`, `ruinedForUnnamed`, `ruinedForUnnamedOpen`, or under a preview `ruinedForPreview`' (V09 §5.8 l. 4019–4020; T-V9-85 'For now: Ruined quarters — a preview'; T-V9-86), then 'Volume 10's explanation renders the same keys (one key, one sentence, J-V9.79)' (l. 3656). repair-r5-V09's HAND-OFFS ask V10 for it: 'V10's explanation of a building under a previewed `disaster` renders `info.crisis.ruinedForPreview`'. repair-r5-V10 lists no hand-off, and V10 names no `ruinedFor` key: §3.9a's disaster bullet (l. 1868–1869) has the clerk tell the look over a building 'from the look read asked with that building … as the look it is', and §3.9b (8) (l. 2033–2035) words each look by its line (`info.crisis.line`, `.lineOpen`, `.lineUnnamed`, `.lineUnnamedOpen`, `.preview`) — 'the words the legend and the why card say (one key, one sentence, J-V9.79)'. For a building the look stands over the why card says 'For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34' and the clerk 'Ruined quarters: the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34': two keys for one case where both units claim one. T-V9-86's V10 clause accepts any `info.crisis.*` key, so nothing tested changes; it is the clerk's wording.
required_change: V10 §3.9a's *A disaster's look* bullet: 'which the clerk tells from the look read asked with that building (its `over`, V10 §3.9b (8)) as the look it is' → 'which the clerk tells from the look read asked with that building (its `over`, V10 §3.9b (8)) as the look it is, in the why card's words: V09's `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in the form matching the look's `says` (`line` → `ruinedFor`, `lineOpen` → `ruinedForOpen`, `lineUnnamed` → `ruinedForUnnamed`, `lineUnnamedOpen` → `ruinedForUnnamedOpen`, `preview` → `ruinedForPreview`; V09 §4.21.12 (4)), its slots the look's'. §3.9b (8) *Explained.*: 'the words the legend and the why card say' → 'the words the legend and the crisis card say, and for a building a look stands over the why card's `ruinedFor` form (V10 §3.9a)'. T-V10-52's building clause: 'tells the look and the house's own damage rows apart' → 'tells the look, worded `info.crisis.ruinedFor`, and the house's own damage rows apart, and under a `disaster` preview a house of its units names it by `info.crisis.ruinedForPreview`'.

claim: Missed subject: `looks`' new `field`, read by V09 and not by V10. R5-08 (c) gave §11.2's `looks` a `field?: Id` (l. 16337–16338), so `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` says whether a famine look draws that field bare (l. 16385). V09 reads it for a field's why card: §4.21.12 (4) (l. 3652–3656) asks `query({ kind: 'looks', view, field })` and adds the `facts` row `info.crisis.ruinedFor` (§5.8; §1b row 377; T-V9-85's 'the why card of a bare field carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'). It then says 'Volume 10's explanation renders the same keys (one key, one sentence, J-V9.79)'. V10's read has no field: `read_map` `look` takes `building?: Ref` only (§2.12 l. 954); `over` is 'with the read's building' (§2.13 l. 1023–1025); §3.5 passes only the input's `building` (l. 1458); §1.2 restates `looks` as asked with a building (l. 189); §3.9b (8) tells only 'A house under a disaster look' (l. 2046); row 34 makes a field passed as `building` answer no `over`. At TOWN to METROPOLIS a field's `why` carries no famine row (V07 §4.5's `VillageField` row serves the village rungs only), and the card's `facts` row is the card's own read, not in the `WhyAnswer` that Ask the assistant sends (V09 §5.8). So for 'why is this field bare?' under a famine, the card names the famine on that field and the clerk cannot tell whether it bares it. That is two units with two outcomes for one case (item 122 (f)), and an input the clerk needs has no producer. R5-08's sweep extended V10 only for the building and the section week.
required_change: V10. (1) §2.12's `read_map` union: `| { kind: 'look'; building?: Ref }` → `| { kind: 'look'; building?: Ref; field?: Ref }`; the comment adds '; with `field`, whether each famine look draws that field bare (§11.2's `looks` member's `field`; §10.2 (d)'s `fields`, (f))'. (2) §2.13's `LookAnswer.crises.looks[].over` comment adds '; with the read's field: `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` — whether this famine look draws that field bare at the drawn week (§10.2 (d)'s `fields`, (f)), evaluated in the generation worker; absent where the read's field names no field (V10 §3.23 row 34)'; the projection comment 'and, with a building, over' → 'and, with a building or a field, over'. (3) §3.5 (l. 1458): after '… and no look carries `over`; V10 §3.23 row 34)' add 'and with its `field` where it names a field (one that names none is not passed)'. (4) §1.2's §11.2 row (l. 189): 'asked with a building each disaster look's `over`' adds 'and with a field each famine look's `over`'. (5) §3.9b (8) adds after *A house under a disaster look*: '*A field under a famine look.* "Why is this field bare?" on a field a famine look draws bare (the look read asked with it answering `over` true; V09 §4.21.12 (4)): the field's own state from its `why`, then the look in the why card's words — `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s form — the bare field leaving with the condition; with `over` false (a field the famine leaves sown), the field's own state alone. At THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the village `WhyProvider`'s row (V07 §4.5) tells it, the read adding none.' (6) Row 34: the edges add 'a read asked with a field — one a famine look draws bare, one it leaves sown; a `field` that names no field (a building, a plot or a district, or a field gone since the read that returned it)'; the outcomes add '`over` true on the famine look, the field told as V09's card tells it; `over` false; `over` absent on every look, every other field as without `field`'. (7) T-V10-52 adds 'on V08 §7.1's famine fixture (T-V9-85's, a famine at severity 0.5), "why is this field bare?" on a bare field names the famine in `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'s form, as its why card's `facts` row does, and on a field left sown names none'; T-V10-50's clause (33) adds the `field` forms.

claim: repair-r5-V09's HAND-OFFS ask V10: 'V10's explanation of a building under a previewed `disaster` renders `info.crisis.ruinedForPreview` (V09 §4.21.12 (4); T-V9-86)'. V09 §4.21.12 (4) makes the why card's `facts` row for a building a disaster look stands over `info.crisis.ruinedFor` 'in the form the line takes' (`ruinedForOpen`, `ruinedForUnnamed`, `ruinedForUnnamedOpen`, under a preview `ruinedForPreview`), and says volume 10 'renders the same keys'. V10 names no `ruinedFor` key: `LookAnswer.looks[].says` carries the legend's line forms only (l. 1015); §3.9b (8)'s *A house under a disaster look* (l. 2046–2051) quotes 'for now its quarter is drawn burned: the Great Fire, weeks 12–20' with no key; C10 says only that the clerk 'tells the drawn ruin as the look's'. The hand-off is not closed at its destination. It is minor: the clerk reads the same look, condition and weeks, and only the catalogue key its sentence renders is unnamed.
required_change: V10. (1) §3.9b (8)'s *A house under a disaster look*: 'then the look — "for now its quarter is drawn burned: the Great Fire, weeks 12–20" —' → 'then the look in the why card's words — `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s form (`ruinedForOpen`, `ruinedForUnnamed`, `ruinedForUnnamedOpen`; under a preview `ruinedForPreview`): "For now: Ruined quarters, the Great Fire, weeks 12–20" —'. (2) C10's outcome 'the clerk tells the drawn ruin as the look's' adds '(`info.crisis.ruinedFor` in its form, V09 §4.21.12 (4))'. (3) T-V10-52 adds 'a building of a previewed `disaster`'s units explained with `info.crisis.ruinedForPreview`, as its why card'.

claim: Round 5 gives V09's why card a famine's bare field (R5-08 (c): §11.2's `looks` `field`, each famine entry's `over`; V09 §4.21.12 (4) l. 3652–3654; row 90), and §4.21.12 (4) closes "Volume 10's explanation renders the same keys" (l. 3656). V10 sends no field (§3.5 l. 1458: a `building` naming none "is not passed"; §3.23 row 34: "a field … `over` absent"), and V10 §3.9b (8) defines only *A house under a disaster look* (l. 2046). At the town rungs the card's famine row is the card's own, read from the `looks` reader, not a `WhyAnswer` row, so the clerk explaining a field under a famine has neither the row nor a read telling a bare field from a sown one: its outcome for "why is this field bare?" is undefined, and it may lay a sown, or seasonally bare (item 117), field to the famine. Off the common path, hence minor.
